newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up in slow start.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up in slow start.

text.p: Mexican stocks notched up marginal gains at the open on Thursday due to bargain-hunting in key blue chips, traders said, adding that dealing was slow while the market awaited news from Wall Street.
"Basically it's up on Telmex, although the market is waiting to see which way the Dow Jones will go. Dealing is slow, mainly in-and-out trading," a desk trader said.
The blue chip IPC index .MXX was up 1.25 points, or 0.03 percent in the opening minutes of trade, at 3,907.50. Trading volume .TV.MX was wafer thin at 684,000 shares.
Market heavyweight Telmex weighed most on the upside, gaining four centavos to 17.22 pesos.
"Telmex closed cheap here yesterday and is just returning to more usual price levels," the trader added.
Dealers noted that other blue chips were dragging the market down, notably Cemex and Grupo Carso.
Cement maker Cemex slid five centavos to 28.55, while holding company Carso was off 10 centavos to 45.35 pesos.
Dealers were divided over the bourse's immediate outlook.
"If it respects support at 3,900 points, then we could extend gains," one desk trader said.
"Blue chips are mixed and there's no volume; I think (early gains) will soon peter out," another trader said.
On the broad market, of a total of 21 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered sliders by five to three.
